title: Hampi vs Varanasi: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Hampi for archaeological wonder and chill. Varanasi for spiritual depth and life-altering intensity. Both are essential India experiences — completely different flavors.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Hampi slightly cheaper at ₹800–1,500/day vs Varanasi's ₹1,000–2,000/day. Both are among India's cheapest destinations.

categories.name: Monuments & UNESCO
categories.summary: Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 1,600+ Vijayanagara Empire remains. Varanasi is not UNESCO-listed.

categories.name: Spiritual Experience
categories.summary: Varanasi is the holiest city in Hinduism — the Ganga Aarti, dawn on the ghats, and the burning ceremonies are transformative.

categories.name: Ease for First-Timers
categories.summary: Hampi is calm, manageable, and accessible. Varanasi is intense and requires some India experience.

categories.name: Food
categories.summary: Hampi wins on setting (riverside cafés). Varanasi wins on food depth (Blue Lassi, kashi chaat, malaiyo).

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Varanasi is easier from North India. Hampi is easier from South India (overnight train from Bengaluru).

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Varanasi: Sarnath. Hampi: Badami-Aihole-Pattadakal Chalukya temples. Both excellent.

categories.name: Crowd Levels
categories.summary: Hampi is low-moderate crowds (backpackers). Varanasi is very crowded year-round with pilgrims and tourists.

faq.question: Is Hampi or Varanasi better for first-time India visitors?
faq.answer: Hampi is more manageable for first-timers. Varanasi is intense and life-altering but better after some India experience.

faq.question: How many days do you need in each?
Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Hampi is slightly cheaper at ₹800–1,500/day vs Varanasi's ₹1,000–2,000/day. Both are exceptional value.
